title: Overview of `XSLmodels`: Importing cross-situational datasets and fitting models
text: package includes several types models: Association-based models: - uncfam() - Uncertainty familiarity biased model - uncfam_attention() - uncfam() learning rate scaled trial uncertainty - uncfam_predictive() - uncfam() added item-level prediction-error term - fazly() - Fazly et al. model - rescorla_wagner() - Rescorla-Wagner model - bayesian_decay() - Bayesian decay model - kalman_filter() - Kalman filter associative model (adaptive, uncertainty-scaled learning rate) Sampling-based models: - uncfam_sampling() - Sampling version uncfam - multi_sampling() - Multi-hypothesis sampling - guess_and_test() - Guess test model - propose_but_verify() - Propose verify model - pursuit() - Pursuit model Reinforcement learning models: - softmax_rl() - Q-learning-style model softmax action selection Bayesian models: - fgt2009() - Frank, Goodman & Tenenbaum (2009) intentional model: joint posterior inference word-object lexicon, marginalizing speaker’s referential intention (batch model; ported wordlearn package). Tune lexicon-size prior fgt2009_sweep_alpha(). - fgt2009_rsa() - fgt2009() Rational Speech Act pragmatic speaker layer Baseline models: - baseline() - Simple co-occurrence baseline - decay() - Decay model - tilles() - Tilles model model can run different parameters compared human data understand learning mechanisms best explain cross-situational word learning behavior.

title: Running and fitting models on naturalistic corpora
text: fgt2009() model built exactly problem: joint posterior inference word–object lexicon whole corpus , marginalizing speaker’s referential intention utterance. batch MCMC model, single run takes seconds minute two corpora (much slower associative tallies) xslFit$matrix holds posterior edge marginals P(word names object | corpus). gamma parameter matters . gamma probability word used referentially. controlled experiment every word label, default gamma = 1. Naturalistic speech full non-referential words (“”, “look”, “”, “see”), corpus wants published gamma = 0.1, kappa = 0.05 – otherwise model forced explain every function word naming something learns almost nothing.
code: res <- xsl_run(   fgt2009(alpha = 3, gamma = 0.1, kappa = 0.05),   rollins_corpus$data ) m_fgt <- res$fits[[1]]$matrix  # the learned lexicon: edges with posterior probability > 0.5 edges <- which(m_fgt > 0.5, arr.ind = TRUE) data.frame(word   = rownames(m_fgt)[edges[, 1]],            object = colnames(m_fgt)[edges[, 2]],            prob   = round(m_fgt[edges], 2)) #>       word object prob #> 1     bear   bear 1.00     # correct #> 2   bottle   bear 1.00     # "baby bottle" co-occurs with the bear #> 3  bigbird   bird 1.00     # correct #> 4     book   book 1.00     # correct #> 5   moocow    cow 1.00     # correct #> 6      hat    hat 1.00     # correct #> 7     oink    pig 1.00     # correct #> ...                        # 28 edges total  get_roc_max(m_fgt, gold_lexicon = rollins_corpus$gold) #> [1] 0.454   # MCMC: expect a little run-to-run variation

text: fgt2009()’s alpha penalizes lexicon size (P(L) proportional exp(-alpha * |L|)) scale corpus size: small gives diffuse -large lexicon, large empty one. F-vs-alpha curve single-peaked, right way “fit” model corpus coarse sweep – [fgt2009_sweep_alpha()] . Pass gold reports best-threshold F-score alpha:  curve rises shallow peak around alpha = 2–4 falls prior forces lexicon empty.
